chinmayananda.title: Chinmayananda on the six questions
chinmayananda.detail: Yudhiṣṭhira, as a righteous man of spiritual inclination, asks a set of questions which the heart of a seeker will always ask. Chinmayananda arranges them as six inquiries: the greatest Lord, the one refuge, whom to glorify, whom to worship, the greatest dharma, and the japa by which a creature goes beyond the bonds of saṃsāra.

chinmayananda.title: Chinmayananda on the installation
chinmayananda.detail: Chinmayananda calls this the “Installation of the Lord.” The seeker sanctifies the body as a divine temple and installs the sacred powers within it. He stresses that the practice points beyond a Lord conceived as separate toward identity without differentiation, while establishing the mood for devoted contemplation.

chinmayananda.english: We meditate upon the Master of the Universe, Lord Viṣṇu, who is ever peaceful, who lies on the great serpent-bed, from whose navel springs the lotus of the creative power, who is the controller of the gods, whose form is the entire universe, who is all-pervading as the sky, of the hue of the cloud, of fascinating beauty, the Lord of Lakṣmī, the lotus-eyed, He who dwells in the hearts of the yogis and who can be approached and perceived through meditation, He who is the destroyer of the fear of saṃsāra.

chinmayananda.title: Chinmayananda on the meditation
chinmayananda.detail: This is meditation upon the form of the Lord. Visualising Him in His all-comprehensive nature, and meditating upon Him, the seeker starts the Viṣṇusahasranāma chanting.
